title: Console: clarify routing fallback label + safer default for demo tenants
author: Chloe Martin
description: Context: During Standard Demo v1 dry runs we repeatedly hit confusion in the Route Editor around what “Fallback” actually does. SEs were narrating it as reliability failover, but the UI label reads like a single generic behavior, and the helper text didn’t distinguish (a) compatibility fallback (e.g., variant/quant profile) from (b) failover when the primary pool is constrained. This led to awkward pauses and a couple of “wait, does it change the model?” questions mid-demo. This PR makes a small copy/label tweak and applies a safer default for demo tenants to prevent accidental cross-region failover in the demo environment. Changes: (1) Rename the Route Editor section label from “Fallback” -> “Failover & Compatibility” and split helper text into two sentences that match talk track terminology (“compatibility fallback” vs “capacity failover”). (2) In the route creation flow, for tenants tagged demo=true, default “Cross-region failover” to OFF (previously inherited the global default). Users can still enable it explicitly. (3) Add an inline warning banner when cross-region failover is enabled: “May route requests to another region when capacity is constrained; verify residency requirements.” (4) Update the internal console strings snapshot + e2e tests that assert labels in the route editor. Notes: This is intentionally a small tweak (no backend behavior changes). Routing policy semantics are unchanged; we’re only clarifying UI and a demo-only default to reduce surprises live. Screenshots: Attached in the PR UI (before/after) showing the Route Editor panel. Test plan: - Console: create route on non-demo tenant -> cross-region failover default unchanged - Console: create route on demo tenant (demo=true) -> cross-region failover default OFF - Toggle cross-region failover -> warning banner appears - Existing routes render correctly with new labels - E2E: console_route_editor_labels.spec passes. Rollout: Safe to ship behind existing feature flag ConsoleRoutingV2; strings will roll with next console deploy. Relates-to: ENG-4924 (dry run hardening) and PM-1842 (deck narrative alignment).
commits: console(routes): rename fallback section + helper copy
console(routes): demo tenant defaults for cross-region failover
test(e2e): update route editor label assertions
review_conversation:
Marissa Cole (requested changes, 2025-08-20): Can we avoid the term “Failover” without specifying capacity? I worry it implies 100% availability guarantees. Suggest: “Capacity failover & compatibility”. Also: helper copy should map 1:1 with talk track (Soojin’s script uses “compatibility fallback” and “capacity failover”).

Chloe Martin (author, 2025-08-20): Good call. I updated label to “Failover & Compatibility” but changed helper to explicitly say “capacity failover”. Added the warning banner copy to avoid over-claiming.

Mina Haddad (routing, 2025-08-20): Defaulting cross-region failover OFF for demo tenants makes sense. Please confirm we’re only changing UI defaults and not mutating backend route objects unexpectedly.

Chloe Martin (author, 2025-08-20): Confirmed. Backend payload only includes crossRegionFailoverEnabled when user toggles it; for demo tenants we initialize the toggle false in the wizard state. Existing routes unaffected.

Sean Gallagher (SRE, 2025-08-21): +1. This reduces demo blast radius. Add a quick note in the banner that cross-region may change latency characteristics.

Chloe Martin (author, 2025-08-21): Added: “May increase latency due to region change” to the warning banner.

Soojin Lee (PMM, 2025-08-21): Thanks. This matches the talk track better; especially the “compatibility fallback” phrasing.

Approvals: Mina Haddad (2025-08-21), Marissa Cole (2025-08-21), Sean Gallagher (2025-08-21).
release_notes: Console: clarified routing UI language for compatibility fallback vs capacity failover; demo tenants now default cross-region failover to off to reduce surprises during live demos.
